methods.ruggedness: Riley, DeGloria and Elliot (1999) terrain ruggedness index
methods.hand: Renno et al. (2008), Nobre et al. (2011)

upstream_area_km2.note: contributing area draining through each cell

drainage.note: cells with at least 0.5 km2 upstream area

drainage_distance_m.note: Euclidean distance to the nearest channel cell

drainage_density.note: channel length per unit area over a 1 km moving window

confluence_density.note: channel junctions per unit area over a 1.5 km moving window

catchment_slope_deg.note: mean slope of the area draining through each cell

landcover_buildable.note: ESA WorldCover classes [30, 40, 50, 60, 100] treated as buildable; [10, 70, 80, 90, 95] excluded

landcover_instability.note: vegetation stability proxy per land cover class

landcover_infiltration.note: infiltration capacity per land cover class, used inverted by the flood model

road_distance_m.note: distance to the nearest of 392 OSM road ways

waterway_distance_m.note: distance to the nearest of 225 OSM waterway ways

terrain_preview.note: Hillshade shaded by elevation, downsampled for the study-area preview. Georeferenced by the study bounding box.

hazard_landslide.note: weighted overlay of 6 normalised factors (drainage_density 0.07, incident_density 0.21, landcover 0.10, rainfall_intensity 0.19, ruggedness 0.13, slope 0.30)

hazard_flood.note: weighted overlay of 4 normalised factors (drainage_distance 0.26, hand 0.42, infiltration 0.12, rainfall_intensity 0.20)

hazard_cloudburst.note: weighted overlay of 4 normalised factors (catchment_steepness 0.26, confluence_density 0.20, extreme_rainfall_frequency 0.30, upstream_area 0.24)

confidence.note: evidence confidence, computed separately and never multiplied into the score

hazard_composite_overlay.note: colour-mapped composite for the map overlay, aligned to the study bbox

red_zones.note: thresholded composite, cleaned to the minimum mapping unit, grown by the configured buffer, exclusive between classes

landcover_ml_buildable.note: Random Forest over Sentinel-2 spectral indices: a second opinion on buildable ground. ESA WorldCover remains the primary path.

confidence_overlay.note: evidence confidence rendered as a diagonal hatch whose density rises as confidence falls; drawn over the hazard surface rather than blended into it, because confidence is never multiplied into the score

landcover_refinement.algorithm: RandomForestClassifier, 250 trees, max depth 10, balanced class weights, CPU only, trained in about a second

labelling_rules.label: water
labelling_rules.reasoning: Cells on the DEM-derived channel network carrying more than 250 km2 of upstream area on near-flat ground: the Alaknanda and its major tributaries, which are permanently wet.

labelling_rules.label: gravel
labelling_rules.reasoning: Flat ground beside smaller channels, 120 to 250 km2 of upstream area: riverbed gravel and braided bar, bare by definition.

labelling_rules.label: snow
labelling_rules.reasoning: Steep ground above 4400 m. In a post-monsoon composite this is snow and ice, and its shortwave signature confirms it.

labelling_rules.label: grass
labelling_rules.reasoning: Gentle ground between 3200 and 3800 m: above the treeline, below permanent snow, the alpine grazing belt.

labelling_rules.label: vegetation
labelling_rules.reasoning: Steep slopes between 1900 and 2900 m more than 1.2 km from any mapped road: the closed-canopy forest belt, too far from access to be cleared.

labelling_rules.label: built
labelling_rules.reasoning: Gentle ground within 60 m of a mapped road where the WorldPop surface exceeds 300 people per square kilometre: settlement and roadside.

labelling_rules.label: cropland
labelling_rules.reasoning: Gentle valley-floor ground between 1000 and 1900 m within 300 m of a road: the terraced cultivation belt.

caveats: Labels come from rules over the DEM, the D8 hydrology, the road network and the WorldPop surface - never from the WorldCover product this model is compared against, which would only prove it can copy.
The rules are approximations. Some labelled cells will be wrong, and the accuracy figures are therefore about the rules as much as the model.
Grass, cropland and built-up are not reliably separable at 30 m. That does not affect the decision this model feeds: all three are buildable, and buildable-or-not is the only question it is asked.
The model refines usable area. It scores no hazard and ranks nothing.
